links.outcome: Output reproducibility (cosine similarity of explanatory text) across 5 repeated runs of the same input
links.effect: General LLMs varied between runs on the same input; the Agentic OODA Framework had less variation, with mean cosine similarity 0.95 versus the general LLMs (Claude, GPT, Llama, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek).
links.quote: In particular, Large Language Model (LLM) based systems often exhibit variability between different runs on the same input, which makes them unsuitable for safety-critical clinical applications.

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) structuring of clinical reasoning with persistent execution states
Similarity-based self-consistency checks on LLM outputs

screen.reason: Evaluates an agentic framework incorporating self-consistency checks, traceable state management, and human-in-the-loop cycles to improve LLM reliability and consistency in clinical decision support for stroke.

primary.practice: multi-agent OODA framework with self-consistency checks and human-in-the-loop verification
